cards.front: Recall a key point about Memory
cards.back: Memory is the process of encoding, storing and retrieving information. Encoding converts sensory input into a storable form; storage retains it; retrieval accesses it when needed.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Memory
cards.back: The Multi-Store Model (Atkinson & Shiffrin, 1968): Sensory memory (brief, capacity limited by senses) -> Short-term memory (limited capacity 7+/-2 items, duration ~30 seconds) -> Long-term memory (potentially unlimited capacity and duration) via rehearsal.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Memory
cards.back: Types of LTM: Episodic (personal experiences, e.g. your first day at school), Semantic (facts and knowledge, e.g. Paris is the capital of France), Procedural (skills and actions, e.g. riding a bike).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Memory
cards.back: Eyewitness testimony is unreliable: Loftus & Palmer (1974) showed leading questions distort recall - participants estimated faster speeds when verbs like 'smashed' were used. Anxiety, weapon focus and post-event discussion also reduce accuracy.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Memory
cards.back: Improving memory: elaborative rehearsal (linking new info to existing knowledge), chunking (grouping items), and mnemonic devices enhance encoding and retrieval.

cards.front: What should you know about psychology exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating memory research, use the GRAVE framework: Generalisability, Reliability, Applications, Validity, Ethics. Always compare lab studies (high control, low ecological validity) with real-world studies (high ecological validity, less control).
